title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
summary: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 π^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 π^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.

title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
comment: 6 pages, including code; the final result remains exactly the same as in the original paper, only the argument changes. Erratum to arXiv:1703.06609
summary: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.

title: A nonarithmetic lattice from a mirror in the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga construction
summary: We prove that the stabilizer of a reflection mirror of the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga lattice $\mathcal{C}(G_{29},3)$ induces a nonarithmetic lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$. This lattice is not commensurable with any Deligne-Mostow lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$ or any lattice in the twenty-two nonarithmetic classes listed by Deraux, Parker and Paupert.

title: Quantitative spectral rigidity for negatively curved manifolds and Outer Space
comment: 19 pages, 2 figures, to appear in Journal of Topology
summary: Let $M$ be a closed manifold with fundamental group $G$. A subset of conjugacy classes $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$ is said to be spectrally rigid if when two negatively curved Riemannian metrics have the same marked length spectra on $E$, then their length spectra agree on all conjugacy classes. In this work we study spectrally rigid subsets from a quantitative perspective. We show that, if the density of $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$, measured with respect to a fixed reference metric, decays more slowly than $T^{-1/2}$ then $E$ is spectrally rigid. We establish analogous rigidity results for Culler-Vogtmann Outer Space and show that the $T^{-1/2}$ threshold is sharp in this setting.

title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
summary: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

title: Minimal quasisections of circle bundles
summary:
Let $E\xrightarrowπB$ be an oriented circle bundle over an oriented closed surface, and let $\mathcal E$ denote its Euler number. A \textit{quasisection} is a smooth surface $Q$, possibly with boundary, together with a generic smooth map $q:Q\to E$ such that $π\circ q(Q)=B$.
  The \textit{local formula} expresses the Euler number $\mathcal E$ of a bundle as a sum of the weights of the \textit{singular vertices} of a quasisection.
  In the present paper determine the minimal number $\mathcal N$ of singular vertices for closed and for bordered quasisections for a given circle bundle. For bordered quasisections, \[
  \mathcal N_{\mathrm b}(E\to B)
  =\left\lceil\frac{3|\mathcal E|}{2}\right\rceil. \] For closed quasisections, If $\mathcal{E}$ is even,
  \[
  \mathcal N_{\mathrm cl}(E\to B)
  =\frac{3|\mathcal E|}{2}. \]
  If $\mathcal{E}$ is odd,
  \[
  \mathcal N_{\mathrm cl}(E\to B)
  =4|\mathcal E|. \]
  We also provide examples of quasisections that realize these minimal values.

title: On the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules
summary: In this paper, we establish several nonvanishing results for Floer lasagna modules $\mathcal{FL}(W,K)$ for a smooth compact connected oriented $4$-manifold $W$ and a knot $K\subset \partial W$, via the evaluation maps to link Floer homology. We first establish a general criterion: if a certain Heegaard Floer cobordism map associated with a smooth $4$-manifold $W$ is nonzero, then $\mathcal{FL}(W,U)\neq 0$, where $U\subset \partial W$ is a local unknot. Applications include the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules for $\#^m\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ and for knot traces $X_n(K)$ when $K$ is slice and $n$ is a non-positive integer. In another direction, we show that for every nontrivial knot $K$ and every integer $n$, the Floer lasagna module $\mathcal{FL}(X_n(K),K_n)$ is nonzero, where $K_n\subset S_n^3(K)$ is the dual knot. Moreover, if $K$ is an L-space knot, then $\mathcal{FL}(X_n(K),K_n)$ is infinite-dimensional for all integers $n\ge \max\{2g(K),1\}$.

title: Casson invariant of knots defined by random braids
summary: We investigate the expectation $E(v_2)$ of the Casson invariant $v_2$ for knots represented by two similar types of braids, the rosette $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $\prod_{1\leq 2i\leq s}σ_{2i}^{\pm 1}\prod_{1\leq 2i+\leq s}σ_{2i+1}^{\pm 1}$ and the quasitoric $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $σ_{1}^{\pm 1}σ_{2}^{\pm 1}...σ_{s-1}^{\pm 1}$. If $k$ is of the form $ns+1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{s+1}{24}$ where $c$ is the number of crossing points of braid; if $k$ is of the form $ns-1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{5-s}{24}$.\\ If we go through all $3$-braids, regardless of the shape of their diagram, we get $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{8}$. \\ For knots with a checkerboard diagram, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{16}$.

title: Lehmer's number is not an orientable stretch factor in genus six
summary: Let $λ_L \approx 1.17628$ be Lehmer's number. We prove that no pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus six with orientable invariant foliations has stretch factor $λ_L$. This gives a negative answer to a question of Lanneau and Thiffeault on the minimal stretch factor in even genus. As a consequence, the minimal stretch factor $δ_6^{+}$ of such maps is the largest root of $x^{12}-x^{9}-x^{7}+x^{6}-x^{5}-x^{3}+1$, approximately $1.20189$. The proof combines the Lefschetz method of Lanneau and Thiffeault, the standardly embedded train tracks of Hironaka and Tsang, an elementary analysis of the transition digraph, and an obstruction from periodic conjugacy classes in the fundamental group.

title: Dimension bounds for finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
summary: We prove that a finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most $81$, substantially improving Prokhorov's bound of $995$. A refinement of Prokhorov's method gives the intermediate bound $162$, while an extension of Vinberg's planar-angle comparison to the finite-volume setting yields the sharper bound. Both arguments combine improved weighting functions with estimates using cusp geometry to control weight contributions of angles at ideal vertices or edges incident to them.

title: Braided Multisections and Aspherical Stein Fillings
summary: We construct Stein fillings diffeomorphic to complements of a connected symplectic unbranched multisection and a regular sphere fiber in the ruled surface $Σ_g\times S^2$. For every $g\geq2$ and every multisection degree $p\geq4$, a fixed contact three-manifold admits infinitely many pairwise nonhomeomorphic aspherical fillings of this form. Their first and second integral homology groups are $\Z^{2g}\oplus\Z/p$ and $\Z^{(2g-1)(p-1)}$, respectively, and their intersection pairings vanish. We vary the braid monodromy while preserving the marked contact boundary. Unbounded torsion orders in the first homology of regular unbranched covers of degree $p2^{p-1}$ detect infinitely many isomorphism types of fundamental groups. We also give an equivariant Weinstein handle construction for the cyclic filling $W_{g,4}$. The contact boundaries are supported by spinal open books with planar pages and have positive ordinary support genus.

title: Relative trisection maps on 4-manifolds
summary: We show that for an arbitrary compact orientable smooth $4$--dimensional manifold $M$ with a given open book structure on the boundary $\partial M \neq \emptyset$, which may be disconnected, there exists a generic smooth map of $M$ onto the $2$--disk which gives a relative trisection on $M$ consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$. This gives a new proof to the existence of a relative trisection on $M$. In fact, it turns out that every relative trisection can be obtained in this way. As a byproduct, we also show that $M$ always admits a decomposition into a PALF (positive allowable Lefschetz fibration) over the $2$--disk $D^2$ and a fiber bundle over the circle with a sutured compression body fiber, consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$ and with the surface bundle structure of the PALF over $\partial D^2$.

title: Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces
summary: Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $ω$ be a smooth positive density, and let $μ$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms. For $g\ge2$ and quasimorphisms vanishing on the disc braid group, we obtain an injective map to $C^0$-continuous homogeneous quasimorphisms on $Homeo_0(N_g,μ)$. We also obtain undistortion criteria in $Homeo_0(N_g)$ and $Diff_0(N_g)$. For $g=1,2$ and every $d\ge2$, we prove $$ \dim\overline H_b^d(Homeo_0(N_g,μ))=\infty,\qquad \dim\overline{EH}_b^d(Diff_0(N_g,ω))=\infty. $$ Moreover, $\overline{EH}_b^d(Homeo_0(N_2,μ))$ is infinite dimensional in every positive even degree $d$. Here $\overline{H}_b^d$ and $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denote reduced bounded cohomology and reduced exact bounded cohomology, respectively.

title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
summary: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park. When $\gcd(p,q)=1$, so that $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot, the formula is a sum of $pr$ monomials with coefficient $+1$, divided by cyclotomic factors, and its exponents are governed by an elementary counting function on the orbit of $q$ modulo $p$. Because the numerator has no cancellation, we are able to give the degree for all $s$ and a simple non-fiberedness criterion.
